title: Primary School Ages 6 to 11
text: Primary School · Ages 6 to 11. Academic rigour built on self-directed inquiry. Authentic Montessori primary education integrated with Ghana Education Service standards. We prepare the reasoning mind for the BECE and beyond.

title: Grades 1-6 GES NaCCA
text: Grades 1–6, Lower & Upper. GES & NaCCA, Aligned.

title: Second Plane of Development
text: The Second Plane of Development. Between six and twelve, children move from the absorbent mind to the reasoning mind. While a preschooler asks "what is it?", a primary child asks "why is it?" and "how does it work?". They are entering a period of enormous intellectual and moral curiosity.

title: Research through work cycles
text: Our primary classrooms meet this curiosity with expansive research. Children follow questions across uninterrupted three-hour work cycles, building collaborative projects that span history, biology, and geometry.

title: Concrete to abstract thinking
text: They transition from concrete materials to abstract thinking—moving from bead frames to written algorithms, from the movable alphabet to expository essays.

title: A comprehensive syllabus
text: A comprehensive syllabus. The Montessori framework delivers the GES curriculum with depth and understanding. Click any subject to explore its progression from concrete materials to abstract reasoning.

title: Mathematics curriculum
text: Mathematics — From physical bead materials to decimal abstraction and algebraic geometry. Golden Bead Materials: Place value built from units, tens, hundreds, thousands — quantity held, then symbolised. Stamp Game & Bead Frames: Operations as physical exchanges — addition, subtraction, multiplication, division checked by the child. Checkerboard & Geometry: Long multiplication on a grid, fraction insets, area models, algebraic binomial/trinomial cubes.

title: Mathematics problem solving
text: Problem Solving & Applications: Word problems, measurement, data handling — mathematics applied to real questions.

title: English Language curriculum
text: English Language — Reading comprehension, grammar analysis, literature, and expository writing. Phonetics & Grammar Analysis: Sandpaper phonograms, movable alphabet, grammar boxes with geometric symbols for parts of speech. Reading & Literature: Phonetic readers to chapter books; book discussions, character studies, comparative analysis.

title: Writing and Oracy
text: Writing Workshop: Expository essays, creative narratives, poetry, research reports — writing as thinking made visible. Oracy & Public Speaking: Prepared addresses, debates, poetry recitation — oratory as a taught competence.

title: Science curriculum
text: Science — Botany, zoology, anatomy, and physical sciences through hands-on experiments. Botany & Zoology: Leaf cabinet, anatomy puzzles, classification by shared characteristics — direct observation first. Human Anatomy & Health: Body systems, nutrition, hygiene — the child as researcher of their own organism.

title: Physical Sciences and Earth
text: Physical Sciences: Magnetism, light, sound, simple machines — experiments designed and interpreted by the child. Earth & Space: Rock cycle, water cycle, solar system — cosmic context for local geography.

title: Ghanaian Language Twi
text: Ghanaian Language (Twi) — Fluency in Twi and appreciation of local literature and cultural context. Oral Proficiency: Conversational Twi, proverbs, storytelling — language as living culture. Reading & Writing: Twi orthography, literature study, composition — literacy in the mother tongue.

title: Twi Cultural Studies
text: Cultural Studies: Adinkra symbols, traditional festivals, Ashanti history — identity rooted in place.

title: Creative Arts
text: Creative Arts — Visual arts, music theory, and performance integrated into academic research. Visual Arts: Drawing, painting, clay, textiles — techniques taught, then applied to illustrate research. Music Theory & Practice: Bells, tone bars, notation, composition — music as mathematical pattern and cultural expression.

title: Drama and Performance
text: Drama & Performance: Class plays, assemblies, presentations — confidence through rehearsed expression.

title: Five Great Lessons intro
text: Cosmic Education. The Five Great Lessons. At the beginning of each year, the primary curriculum is introduced through five impressionistic stories that spark imagination and set the context for all future studies.

title: Story of the Universe and Life
text: Story of the Universe — Creation, astronomy, chemistry, and earth sciences. Story of Life — Biology, botany, zoology, and evolution of living things.

title: Stories of Humans Writing Numbers
text: Story of Humans — History, culture, invention, and human resilience. Story of Writing — Communication, language arts, reading, and literature. Story of Numbers — Mathematics, geometry, trade, and engineering.

title: Campus Life
text: Campus Life. Classrooms that open onto outdoor space for movement and practical stewardship of the environment.

title: Preparation for the BECE
text: The Pathway Forward. Preparation for the BECE. The three-hour work cycle gives students the stamina for sustained, exam-driven workload of Junior High. By the time they reach JHS, self-directed study is second nature.

title: BECE progression steps
text: Lower Primary — Basic 1-3 (Ages 6-8). Upper Primary — Basic 4-6 (Ages 9-11). Junior High — JHS 1-3 (Ages 12-14). BECE — National Exams.
